title_zh: 成就系统的完整实现：从数据模型到前端弹窗，游戏化留存全解析
title_en: Achievement System: From Data Model to Unlock Popups — Complete Gamification Implementation
desc_zh: 成就系统是我平台上对留存率影响最大的单一功能。这篇文章完整拆解了成就系统的实现：数据模型设计、条件评估引擎、解锁时机、前端弹窗、以及我踩过的那些坑——为什么成就不能在前端判断、为什么条件逻辑不能写死在代码里。
desc_en: The achievement system is the single feature with the largest measurable impact on retention on my platform. This article fully breaks down the implementation: data model design, condition evaluation engine, unlock timing, frontend popup animations, and the mistakes I made — why achievements can't be evaluated on the frontend, and why condition logic can't be hardcoded.
content_en:
## Why Achievements Improve Retention Before adding achievements, my platform's retention was: - Day 1: 52%, Day 7: 18%, Day 30: 6% Three months after launch: - Day 1: 58%, Day 7: 27%, Day 30: 11% Day 30 retention nearly doubled. The reason is simple: **achievements give users a reason to come back.** Even on days they don't want to play long, they'll open a few rounds to chase a nearly-unlocked achievement. --- ## Data Model ```go type Achievement struct { ID string `gorm:"primaryKey"` // e.g., "speed_demon" GameID string `gorm:"index"` // empty = platform-wide TitleZH string TitleEN string Icon string Rarity string // "common" | "rare" | "epic" | "legendary" Points int Hidden bool Conditions string `gorm:"type:jsonb"` // unlock conditions as JSON } ``` Conditions are stored as JSON, not hardcoded: ```json { "type": "and", "conditions": [ { "type": "game_id", "value": "sudoku" }, { "type": "difficulty", "value": "hard" }, { "type": "time_lt", "value": 300 }, { "type": "result", "value": "win" } ] } ``` Why JSON instead of hardcoded logic? Adjusting unlock conditions only requires a database update, not a redeployment. --- ## Condition Evaluation Engine ```go func EvaluateCondition(cond map[string]interface{}, result GameResult, history UserHistory) bool { switch cond["type"] { case "game_id": return result.GameID == cond["value"] case "difficulty": return result.Difficulty == cond["value"] case "result": return result.Result == cond["value"] case "time_lt": return result.Duration < int(cond["value"].(float64)) case "win_streak": return history.WinStreak(result.GameID) >= int(cond["value"].(float64)) case "total_games": return history.TotalGames(result.GameID) >= int(cond["value"].(float64)) case "and": for _, sub := range cond["conditions"].([]interface{}) { if !EvaluateCondition(sub.(map[string]interface{}), result, history) { return false } } return true case "or": for _, sub := range cond["conditions"].([]interface{}) { if EvaluateCondition(sub.(map[string]interface{}), result, history) { return true } } return false } return false } ``` Nested `and`/`or` supports arbitrarily complex unlock conditions. --- ## Why Achievements Can't Be Evaluated on the Frontend My initial idea was to evaluate achievements in JavaScript — one fewer API call. **Three reasons this is wrong:** 1. **Frontend code can be modified.** Users can manipulate JavaScript to unlock any achievement. 2. **History data lives on the server.** "Win 5 consecutive games" requires database queries. 3. **Multi-device consistency.** Frontend evaluation across devices produces inconsistent records. All achievement evaluation happens server-side. Non-negotiable. --- ## Frontend: Unlock Popup Animation The visual reward moment must feel significant — it's the "you won something" instant. ```html @if (notify.current(); as ach) {
{{ ach.icon }}
🏆 Achievement Unlocked!
{{ ach.titleEN }}
{{ ach.descEN }}
+{{ ach.points }} pts
} ``` ```css @keyframes slide-up { from { transform: translateY(100%); opacity: 0; } to { transform: translateY(0); opacity: 1; } } .animate-slide-up { animation: slide-up 0.35s cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1) forwards; } ``` Auto-dismissed after 5 seconds. If multiple achievements unlock simultaneously, they queue and display sequentially. --- ## Hidden Achievements: The Surprise Effect Hidden achievements don't appear in the achievement list until unlocked. Examples: - **Night Owl**: play between 1-4 AM - **Speed Demon**: win 3 consecutive games in under 2 minutes each - **Explorer**: try every game on the platform These spread by word-of-mouth — players discover them and share them. The surprise factor is the marketing mechanism. --- *Next: **[12] Monetization** — how to make money from an indie game platform without destroying the user experience.*
